chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the boy reaches ten years, his bequest is valid.'
ai.seo_question: At what age is a boy's will considered valid in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the age of seven to ten as the threshold for a child's limited legal capacity (ahliyyat al-adā') to make a bequest, reflecting the Shia juristic view that discernment (tamyīz) begins around this age. It highlights the practical implication that while a boy is not yet fully mature, his testamentary dispositions are recognized and enforceable, distinguishing this stage from the complete legal capacity attained at puberty.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abdullah who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the boy reaches ten years, his bequest is allowed’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from certain persons of his people from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has narrated the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When a boy becomes ten years old his will is permissible.’”
